modules.about:
MODERN ART™

MONDRIAN generates homages to the work of the Dutch painter Piet Mondrian (1872-1944). These images more closely resemble the work of Mondrian's colleague, Theo van Doesberg, who painted the same stuff but never seemed to get it quite right.
ROTHKO generates displays not dissimilar from the work of the Russian-born American Abstract Expressionist painter Mark Rothko (1903-1970).
POLLOCK reminds us ever so slightly of the work of Jackson Pollock (1912-1956), the American Abstract Expressionist drip painter.

Splotch artwork by Igor Gasowski (1957- ).

The mowing ritual was strangely compelling to all of us at Berkeley Systems since we haven't even seen grass since the beginning of the great drought and the end of the 60's.

modules.about:
MAJOR METAPHYSICAL APPLIANCES™

Do the appliances in your home exist when unplugged from the space-time grid? Are Platinum and Toast just thin, washable enamel coatings keeping us from seeing the Essential Transcendent Beingness of the so-called “universe”?

This meditation on the deep Connections between Existence and Convenience was submitted to the 1992 After Dark Contest by Gregory M. Becker. It was rewritten by Andy Karn, with art by Igor Gasowski and Tomoya Ikeda. This sentence is false.

modules.about:
PEARLS™

Pearls is an abstract graphical pattern that is drawn according to simple rules: A single square is created. Squares half as big are put on top of the original square, and the process repeats. This gives Pearls the “fractal” property that it contains smaller and smaller copies of itself.

You can choose from a dozen different Decorations of the squares, or choose Random to decorate them unpredictably. No square is drawn smaller than the number of pixels set with the Detail slider. After it’s done, the picture will stay up for the amount of time set with the Pause slider.
modules.credits:
Pearls by Andy Karn.
©1992 Berkeley Systems Inc.

Photon keeps things active (radioactive?) with bursts of various sorts - photons, sort of squiggly outward bursts; electrons, spinning around the center; protons, spiralling outwards; and neutrinos, bursting straight out the center.

"Length" sets the length of the trails.
"Burst Delay" sets the amount of time between bursts.
"Always Centered" keeps the bursts always centered on the screen.
"Burst" allows you to select the type of bursts.

ROSE

Rose was first conceived, in a rudimentary way, on an IBM PC in BASIC many years ago, soon after the IBM had first hit the market.

Some years later I remembered the algorithm and re-created the code (which had long since been lost). Then I forgot about it again until After Dark came out and, once again, I remembered it. The code was converted to After Dark mainly by Bruce Burkhalter.

It's based on trigonometry, that most hated and most beautiful of mathematical subjects.
